changes: Added hard Codex adapter capabilities: koala-codex doctor/verify diagnostics, Codex process-event session telemetry, init --verify-codex wrapper verification, fresh-init local bin/koala.js plus bin/koala-codex.js, stale evidence rejection, and regression tests/docs for these paths.
usage: Use node bin/koala-codex.js doctor for live Codex diagnostics, node bin/koala-codex.js verify_codex or node bin/koala.js verify_codex for scriptable evidence, and npx koala-init --verify-codex or node bin/koala.js init --verify-codex to generate and verify Codex assets in a new project.
expectedOutcome: Codex users can initialize or run Koala without fake .Codex/hooks/settings assets; doctor and verify commands give executable hard evidence, and REVIEW/DONE gates reject missing, failing, or stale Codex evidence.
actualTranscript: node bin/koala-codex.js doctor and verify_codex both reported Codex adapter checks passed 7/7. Fresh init --verify-codex generated bin/koala.js and bin/koala-codex.js, verified local wrapper heartbeat, and the generated wrapper ran session_brief under minimal PATH without relying on global koala.
outcomeDiff: No remaining difference: expected hard executable Codex behavior matches actual transcript.
pitfalls: The main trap was treating bare global koala as equivalent to the local Codex wrapper; stale/core-only global installs can hide missing commands, so generated wrappers and docs must prefer verified local executable paths.
